title: Primary vs persistent: who lives in the canal
topic: How the flora of an untreated necrotic pulp differs from that of a previously treated tooth, and where E. faecalis really stands.

claims.claim: PRIMARY = untreated necrotic pulp; PERSISTENT = survived treatment; SECONDARY = got in during or after treatment
claims.source: Siqueira JF Jr & Rôças IN, J Oral Microbiol 2009;1:2009 (PMID 21523208; full text)

claims.claim: Primary infection: 10-20 taxa per canal (molecular studies)
claims.source: Siqueira JF Jr & Rôças IN, J Oral Microbiol 2009;1:2009 (PMID 21523208; full text, text and Table 1; review-level range)

claims.claim: Primary deck: Gram-negative and Gram-positive genera mixed, nine anaerobes and one facultative Streptococcus (genus names, Gram colour, anaerobe/facultative badges)
claims.source: Genus lists and Gram: Siqueira & Rôças, J Oral Microbiol 2009 (PMID 21523208); mix dominated by obligate anaerobes: Figdor D & Sundqvist G, Aust Dent J 2007;52(1 Suppl):S38-51 (PMID 17546861); per-genus oxygen tolerance and shape: abstracts listed in NOTES.md

claims.claim: Treatment removes most of the deck; what is left is mostly Gram-positive (two violet cards cross the line)
claims.source: Siqueira JF Jr & Rôças IN, J Endod 2008;34:1291-1301.e3 (PMID 18928835; abstract)

claims.claim: Previously treated tooth: 1-5 taxa per canal (adequately treated; culture + PCR)
claims.source: Siqueira JF Jr & Rôças IN, J Oral Microbiol 2009;1:2009 (PMID 21523208; full text); Siqueira JF Jr et al., PLoS One 2016;11:e0162887 (PMID 27689802; full text)

claims.claim: E. faecalis: often found, rarely dominant; qPCR, 29 teeth: found in 11, dominant in 1
claims.source: Rôças IN & Siqueira JF Jr, J Clin Microbiol 2012;50:1721-4 (PMID 22403423; full text); 'often found' = prevalence 24-77%: Stuart CH et al., J Endod 2006;32:93-8 (PMID 16427453)

claims.claim: Primary: mostly obligate anaerobes, Gram - and +
claims.source: Figdor D & Sundqvist G, Aust Dent J 2007;52(1 Suppl):S38-51 (PMID 17546861); Byström A & Sundqvist G, Scand J Dent Res 1981;89:321-8 (PMID 6947391)

claims.claim: Persistent/secondary: more facultatives, mostly Gram + (culture findings), sometimes yeast
claims.source: Pinheiro ET et al., Int Endod J 2003;36:1-11 (PMID 12656508); Molander A et al., Int Endod J 1998;31:1-7 (PMID 9823122); Siqueira & Rôças, J Oral Microbiol 2009 (PMID 21523208); yeast: Mergoni G et al., J Endod 2018;44:1616-1625.e9 (PMID 30241680)

claims.claim: Culture + PCR picture; sequencing finds more in both
claims.source: Siqueira JF Jr et al., PLoS One 2016;11:e0162887 (PMID 27689802); Manoil D et al., Proteomics Clin Appl 2020;14:e1900060 (PMID 31950679)

claims.source: Toy model / schematic: labelled on screen 'schematic decks'; icons are textbook morphology, not to scale

caption:
Who lives in the canal? Depends on whether the tooth was treated.

Primary (untreated necrotic pulp): about 10-20 taxa per canal in molecular studies, mostly obligate anaerobes, Gram - and +.
Previously treated: 1-5 taxa if adequately treated, more facultatives, mostly Gram + by culture, sometimes yeast.
Persistent = survived treatment; secondary = got in during or after it.
E. faecalis: by qPCR in 11 of 29 treated teeth, dominant in 1. Sequencing finds more taxa in both.

Refs: Siqueira & Rôças 2009, J Oral Microbiol; Rôças & Siqueira 2012, J Clin Microbiol; Siqueira 2016, PLoS One
